remediations.exact_change: ansible.builtin.file with parameterised owner and mode
remediations.service_risk: HIGH IF HARD-CODED. nginx runs as the nginx user and must retain read access. mode 0600, chown root:root, or a blanket chmod 0640 across /srv all break the web check. The rule's own rationale states that files "can be configured using a combination of user and group permissions to support whatever legitimate access is needed" - so the control is applied with parameters, not a blanket lockdown. SELinux context httpd_sys_content_t must also be preserved (see DL-004).

remediations.finding: ASLR setting is correct at runtime but not persisted
preconditions: sysctl kernel.randomize_va_space; grep -r randomize_va_space /etc/sysctl.conf /etc/sysctl.d/ 2>/dev/null || echo 'not persisted'
remediations.verified_baseline: CORRECTED AFTER VERIFICATION. kernel.randomize_va_space already reads 2 in the running kernel, so the original precheck ("value is not 2") was wrong. The rule fails because no file under /etc/sysctl.d/ declares the value. The control gap is durability: nothing guarantees the setting after a reboot or after another package writes a conflicting value.

remediations.finding: Loopback interface not assigned to the trusted zone
remediations.exact_change: Add lo to the trusted zone; add rich rules dropping spoofed loopback sources on other interfaces. No package installation required.
validation: test_loopback_trusted AND test_spoofed_loopback_dropped AND test_web_service_responds AND test_no_new_listening_ports
remediations.rollback: Remove lo from the trusted zone and remove the rich rules, returning firewalld to its baseline configuration (public zone on eth0, trusted zone empty).
remediations.desired_state: Interface lo assigned to the trusted zone; traffic with a 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1 source arriving on eth0 is dropped.
remediations.verified_baseline: CORRECTED AFTER VERIFICATION. firewalld-1.2.5-2.el9_3 is already installed and active. Original design assumed it needed installing. Active zones: public (eth0), trusted (no interfaces). The trusted zone exists with target ACCEPT but lo is not assigned to it, and no rich rules drop spoofed loopback sources on eth0.
remediations.service_risk: THIS IS THE SERVICE-CONFLICT CONTROL. A naive reading of "restrict loopback traffic" blocks 127.0.0.1 entirely, which kills the web check (curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:8080/) and constitutes a forbidden regression. The rule's rationale is two-sided: TRUST lo, RESTRICT spoofed loopback sources arriving elsewhere. Correct parameterisation applies the control and keeps the service green. No new listening port is opened, so forbidden_regressions is respected.
remediations.expected_scanner_effect: both firewalld loopback rules move fail -> pass
